sections.h2: Who records deeds in Crawford County, Pennsylvania?
sections.html:
The Register of Wills and Recorder of Deeds office does, and one office covers both jobs. Weekday hours run from 8:30 in the morning until 4:30 in the afternoon, and the phone number is 814-373-2537. Recorded land records include deeds, mortgages, mortgage satisfactions and releases, agreements such as oil and gas leases, UCC filings, notary publics and powers of attorney.

Records are searchable online back to 1954, and land records exist back to 1800. The office warns that data from 1954 through 1974 is under review for accuracy, so it advises checking the index books in the office for older entries. Copies requested in writing cost $0.50 a page.

The office also offers a free property fraud monitoring program through its Landex software, which an owner can sign up for to be alerted when something is recorded against the property.

sections.h2: How much is a deed filing in Crawford County?
sections.html:
A deed is $74.75 and a mortgage is $74.75 on the schedule effective November 17, 2025. Those prices include four pages and four names to be indexed; each extra name is $0.50 and each extra page is $2.00.

The office accepts an overpayment of $5.00 or less and records it as an overpayment on the receipt. A mailed package should include at least $1.00 for postage and a return envelope, or a self-addressed stamped envelope. The county's website also hosts a fee calculator for the main recording documents.

sections.h2: What is the Uniform Parcel Identifier rule in Crawford County?
sections.html:
A UPI number is required on every document the county's ordinance covers before it can be recorded. The Crawford County Commissioners adopted the ordinance, and it took effect November 29, 2018. The fee is $20.00 for each parcel that receives a number, paid at recording, and it may go on the same check as the recording fee.

For a house sale, that means the deed's parcel has to carry a UPI before the recorder will take it. Request the number before closing day. A seller closing without one should phone the office on 814-373-2537 and ask how to get the parcel numbered.

The county made one other change that sellers sometimes miss. Since September 20, 2018 it no longer requires a separate check for the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax, so the tax does not need a check of its own. The Department of Revenue explains that the state tax is 1 percent of the value, buyer and seller are both liable, and local governments often add their own tax.

sections.h2: How do I record a Crawford County deed electronically?
sections.html:
The office lists four electronic recording companies, so a title company can usually send a deed without a courier.

  • Simplifile, at 800-460-5657 or simplifile.com.
  • EPN, at 888-325-3365.
  • CSC, at 866-652-0111 or erecording.com.
  • Indecomm Global Services, at 877-272-5250.

E-recorded Statement of Value forms carry a small extra charge: the office now charges $0.50 per page for any document attached to the form, and the amount is calculated automatically.

sections.h2: What if the Crawford County house belongs to an estate?
sections.html:
The same office holds the Register of Wills, so an heir can open the estate and later record the deed from one location. The Register of Wills probates estates, collects Pennsylvania inheritance tax and takes the resident inheritance tax returns. When an estate is opened, a death certificate must be filed along with a $7.00 filing fee, a rule the office dates to February 3, 2020.

  • All estates on file are public record, and estate records from 1991 to the present are online.
  • Probated estates go back to 1800, including most of the old original wills and supporting papers.
  • Will indexes cover 1800 to 1974 and 1975 to 2000.
  • Copies mailed or faxed on written request are $0.50 a page with the fees.

Once the estate has authority to sell, the sale follows the usual recording steps, including the UPI number and the Statement of Value when the transfer is not a paid sale.

sections.h2: What does Crawford County look like for a seller?
sections.html:
Crawford County was created on March 12, 1800 from part of Allegheny County and named for Colonel William Crawford. It covers 1,012 square miles of land in the northwest corner of the state, with Meadville as the county seat. Meadville had 13,388 residents in 2010, and Titusville, the other city, had 5,601. Cambridge Springs, Cochranton, Linesville and Saegertown are among the boroughs.

Pymatuning State Park sits on Pymatuning Reservoir, and Conneaut Lake is one of the boroughs. The county forms the Meadville micropolitan area, part of the larger Erie-Meadville combined statistical area. The abolitionist John Brown lived in the county for 11 years, and the John Brown Farm, Tannery and Museum recalls his tannery there.

The Census Bureau estimated 81,792 residents in July 2025, a decrease of 2.6 percent from the 2020 base. In Meadville, the average temperature runs from 24.9 degrees Fahrenheit in January to 69.5 in July.

sections.h2: What should a Crawford County seller bring to the closing?
sections.html:
A tidy package keeps the deed from bouncing.

  • The signed, notarized deed with the buyer's address.
  • The UPI number for the parcel and $20.00 to cover the fee.
  • A check for the recording fee from the November 17, 2025 schedule, with state and local transfer tax.
  • A Statement of Value if tax is excused or not paid in full.
  • Postage and a return envelope for mailed packages.

Recording is the final step, but the tax and fee amounts depend on the sale price, so the title agent should run the numbers in advance.

faqs.q: What is the filing charge for a Crawford County deed?
faqs.a: A deed is $74.75 under the schedule effective November 17, 2025, covering four pages and four names. Extra names are $0.50 each and extra pages $2.00 each.

faqs.q: What is the UPI fee in Crawford County?
faqs.a: It is $20.00 for each parcel that receives a number, paid when the document is recorded. The ordinance took effect November 29, 2018, and the fee can go on the same check as the recording fee.

faqs.q: Does Crawford County want a check just for transfer tax?
faqs.a: No. The office says that since September 20, 2018 it no longer requires separate checks for the Pennsylvania realty transfer tax.

faqs.q: Can a Crawford County deed be recorded electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The office lists Simplifile, EPN, CSC and Indecomm Global Services as electronic recording companies.

faqs.q: How far back can I search Crawford County records online?
faqs.a: Recorder of Deeds records are online from 1954 to the present, and land records exist back to 1800. The office advises checking the index books for the 1954 to 1974 period.
